verdict: Lend selectively in Warangal rice milling only to non-CMR, own-account millers with clean books and verified paddy sourcing; avoid any borrower touched by the CMR diversion probe.
title: Warangal Rice Milling & Export: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Warangal rice mill buys paddy, dries and de-husks it, and sells rice, bran and husk; cash comes back only after the rice is sold, so the mill is a working-capital machine, not an asset play.** The miller's margin is the difference between paddy cost and rice realisations plus by-product income; power, labour and drying add cost, and the mill has little pricing power because rice is a commodity. **So when a proposal lands, check the paddy procurement source and the by-product (bran, husk) offtake first; if the mill cannot show where paddy comes from and who buys bran, ask for the last six months of purchase and sale invoices.**

## What has broken now
**The local shock is legal, not commercial: the CID is arresting rice millers in the CMR (custom-milled rice) cases, with four more arrests in Mulugu and 11 absconding, and over 300 petitions filed in the High Court seeking protection [1].** The allegation is that millers sold fine-variety paddy allotted by the government in the open market and supplied cheaper coarse rice in its place [3]; 17 millers were untraceable after a message circulated [2]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower or any promoter is named in the CMR probe; if yes, decline, and if the mill does government CMR work at all, ask for the allotment and delivery records before anything else.**

## Where the growth is
**The Telangana backdrop is genuinely strong: GST collections are up 13.8% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and electricity demand is up 15.7% against India's 9.5% [D].** Peer results confirm rice demand is healthy: KRBL reported Basmati exports up about 8% year-on-year to 6.5 million metric tons and a record domestic quarter up 22% [4], and its Q1 FY2027 EBITDA margin was 23.8% against 13.9% [7]; Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar's Q1FY26 net profit rose 94% with revenue up 55% [6]. **So pursue own-account millers and exporters with branded or export-linked rice, clean CMR-free books and steady bran offtake; avoid millers whose business is mainly government CMR allotment.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle: a cash-credit or bill-discounting limit sized to the paddy-to-rice cycle, not a term loan for a new mill.** Take monthly stock and book-debt statements, monthly GST returns, and a quarterly check that paddy purchases match milling output. **If the borrower's export receivables are in foreign currency, ask for the hedging policy, because ICRA flags foreign-currency risk on export receivables [9].** Rating commentary expects 6-8% revenue growth in FY2026 on export and domestic demand [8], so size limits to that, not to the 26.3% bank credit growth against 5.1% output [D].

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for paddy purchase invoices that do not match milling volumes, sudden shifts to coarse rice supply, and any CID or High Court notice [1][3].** Also watch bran offtake stopping and stock ageing past one season. **If any of these appear, freeze the limit and ask for the CMR allotment file; if the borrower is named in the probe, exit.**
